pageCache.text:
About Meridian School
Hello and a warm welcome to our website which aims to give you a flavour of our successful one form entry primary school. We are a creative and inclusive learning community which values individuality and celebrates differences. Nestled between Greenwich Park and the River Thames, we are uniquely placed to make learning exciting, fun and relevant. The Meridian Line runs through the very centre of our school and from our rooftop Arts studio children and staff have the privilege of teaching and learning in view of Greenwich’s World Heritage site.
Our children, from Nursery to Year 6, come from richly diverse backgrounds with about 40 languages spoken, and our intake is complemented by a Local Authority Designated Provision (LARP) for up to 12 deaf children. We have high aspirations for each and every child and our experienced and committed staff team empower children to become confident, independent and resilient learners who make excellent progress and achieve very well during their time with us.
We believe positive relationships and a caring ethos are the basis for great learning and work hard to foster a sense of belonging for all our children. We value our partnerships with parents/carers.
We are part of a small federation with Robert Owen Nursery School and members of the GCSP (Greenwich Community Schools Partnership) - a large group of maintained primary, nursery, special and secondary schools who work together for the benefit of all our children.
Do enjoy looking around our website and finding out more about us. We look forward to welcoming you in person.
Best wishes, Jo Graham, Executive Headteacher

Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club runs from 7.30am each morning and is supervised by two experienced members of staff, Mark & Nealam.
There are two types of bookings:
Children receive a breakfast followed by a programme of leisure/learning activities until 8.45am, when they go to the playground with other children until the bell rings at 8.50am.
All children must be pre-registered before attending the club. Parents who wish to apply for a Breakfast Club place should contact school office staff.
We accept payment for Breakfast Club via Parent Pay or Childcare Vouchers. Our unique reference number is 100137. Please contact finance@meridian.greenwich.sch.uk if you would like further information regarding using Childcare Vouchers.
If there is demand for more places than we have space for, then we may have to prioritise places for parents/carers who are working or studying.
If you would like your child to attend, please contact the school office to enquire about availability and booking arrangements.
If you need to contact Breakfast Club between 7.30am and 8.00am, please use the following number: 07399 009572
Breakfast Club information for parents

Our Governors
School Governors play a key role in overseeing the management of the school. Their main responsibilities include planning the budget, recruitment and appointment of staff and the development and implementation of policies in consultation with staff and parents.
Meridian Governing Body is currently composed of Parent Governors, the Executive Headteacher, a staff Governor, a Governor nominated by the Local Authority and co-opted Governors chosen to reflect the local community and who bring a range of skills, experience and expertise to the role.
Much of the work of the Governing Body is done by sub-committees whose recommendations and decisions are verified by the main Governing Body. Extra people who are not Governors can be co-opted onto sub-committees.
The current range of sub-committees is:
• Business • Curriculum • Personnel and Legal
All Governors aim to visit the school regularly, usually with a specific brief to examine one or more areas of school life in some detail. Many are in school on a daily basis and have a close involvement with everything that goes on.
The school is always keen to hear from anyone who is prepared to be a Governor or would like to join a sub-committee. Please contact the Executive Headteacher to discuss any opportunities for greater involvement in the running of the school.
Please click here for details of the members of the Governing Body.

After School Clubs
After School Clubs Timetable
There is no cost for Young Researchers, Drama Club or KS2 Choir.
Sports clubs cost £4 per session and will be listed on ParentPay. The cost for the whole term (£40 for 10 weeks) will appear, and you can choose to pay it off all at once or make a payment of £4 weekly.
When will clubs run from and until, and what time will they start and finish?
Following the timetable above, all clubs will usually run for 10 weeks per term. Each club will start at the end of the school day and finish at 4:20pm. Please ensure that your child is collected on time.
How can I sign my child up for a club, and how will spaces be allocated?
Parents are emailed at the start of each term (Autumn, Spring, Summer) a google form to sign up for clubs for the whole term. You must reapply for clubs each term, if you would like your child to continue attending.
Please email the school office sao@meridian.greenwich.sch.uk if you wish to sign up after the google form closes.
Children who applied for a place at a club at the beginning of the previous Term who were not successful will be prioritised for places. After that, places will be allocated on a first come, first served basis.

Our Curriculum
Underpinned by our whole school values, our rich, broad and balanced curriculum is holistic in nature - we aim to enthuse children about learning and support them in developing the skills, attitudes and knowledge which will enable them to make excellent progress, both academically and socially & emotionally, and which will enable them to be resilient, independent learners, prepared for future learning and life.
Please click on the 'Our Curriculum' link to read about our curriculum vision; click on the termly overviews below to see what is taught for each year in each subject within the school and on the 'Meridian Mini-Guide' to read more information about how we implement the curriculum.
Our curriculum works on a two year rolling cycle (Year A and Year B). This means that two of our classes will be studying the same topic at any one time. The advantages of this are that, in our one-form entry school, teachers are able to plan lessons together. Collaborating together allows staff to plan these lessons with a more reflective approach, and share trips between paired year groups. We also find it allows children to consolidate their learning by discussing it with peers outside of their own class.
To find out more information about our curriculum, please contact Jeff Mason, our Curriculum Leader via the School Office.
Links to the National Curriculum and Early Years Curriculum are also available here.
Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised is a complete systematic synthetic phonics programme (SSP) which is used at Meridian.

Homework
At Meridian, homework reinforces learning which has already taken place in class. It should be a positive experience for your child and we reward completed homework as part of class reward schemes. (We do not however apply sanctions for homework not completed). Meridian is committed to providing an inclusive and dyslexia friendly environment, and homework for all children, including those with SEN, will be appropriate to their levels and accessible to them.
Reading— We encourage parents to put aside some time to read with their child as often as possible. Short bursts of 10-20 minutes usually work best but even a few minutes are valuable. Each year children are given a new reading diary. Parents can use this to comment on their child’s reading. Children can also make their own comments and there are activities which children can complete. Staff will check the diary each week. It is intended to last the whole year so parents can decide how often to use it.
Children are encouraged to bring home two books at a time – one is a ‘levelled book’ with a coloured sticker which children should be able to read independently, the other is a book of their choice which you may like to read to them. Children can change their books as often as necessary – staff support this process and you are welcome to do the same before and after school. All children should have a book bag to bring books and diaries to and from school and should bring this book bag to school every day.
Spellings – Children across the school are taught phonics and spelling patterns and carry out spelling investigations. There are some words which need to be taught by the shape of the whole word - words which arise frequently in the English language but which cannot be sounded out – such as ‘their’. Each week, children in Year 1 upwards are given new spellings to practise in class. A copy of spellings is sent home each week and we appreciate parents support in practising these with children. (We prioritise phonics/spelling patterns and the high frequency words. For children who are making good progress with these, we may send home topic words or spelling errors spotted in class.)
Literacy and Maths homework – Children in Y2 upwards are set a piece of Literacy or Maths homework every Friday. This is recorded in a homework book and should be handed in by the following Wednesday. We feel that about 20 minutes is a reasonable length of time for a Year 2 child to spend on homework, 30 minutes in Y3-Y5 and about 40 minutes in Y6. This is a guide – parents know their child. If a child is ever struggling with a piece of homework, parents are asked to leave it and have a chat with the class teacher. We use an online ‘Mathletics’ scheme across the school for Reception upwards which children can access at home and which allows them to compete with children across the world!
Any real maths or writing opportunities which parents/carers can carry out with children are always valuable – making shopping lists; writing cards; emailing family and friends; counting out coins; weighing ingredients; adding up shopping in the supermarket… Class teachers will be happy to give parents/carers more ideas.
Other homework - Teachers occasionally set additional homework based around a project. SEAL (Social and Emotional Aspects of Learning) activities are sometimes sent home.
